recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR-43167. Handle future THO migration or broader DeviceDefinition terminology cleanup separately under FHIR-55255 if and when it reaches an applied/published state.
issue_request: FHIR-43167 was an Applied/Persuasive OO change request for R6 asking that DeviceDefinition.productionIdentifierInUDI use an extensible binding to Device Production Identifier in UDI and include language that jurisdictions may define other production identifier types and indicate required identifiers through regulation or implementation guidance.
initial_application: The productionIdentifierInUDI element came from FHIR-34348, whose Published resolution described an extensible binding, but the initial source implementation used code with a required binding. FHIR-43167 was later applied by commit 964bed35ae16b592f615007c17d9d4c6a82464db, changing the element to CodeableConcept with an extensible binding, and by commit c7415b5df97563f5f20fe6e183a942c176db0f73, adding the requested jurisdictional comment.
additional_context: DeviceDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/devicedefinition/structuredefinition-DeviceDefinition.xml is in build scope. Current source preserves the requested CodeableConcept type, extensible binding, and jurisdictional comment. OO minutes from 2023-12-07 record FHIR-43167 in the accepted block vote. Later FHIR-55255 is related to broader DeviceDefinition terminology and possible THO migration, but it is only Resolved - change required and does not create an Applied/Published contradiction for this seed.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative current source already satisfies both parts of FHIR-43167, and generated-looking SVG artifacts or redundant prose do not require edits for this issue.

related_jiras.note: Introduced DeviceDefinition.productionIdentifierInUDI and explains why the pre-FHIR-43167 source had a binding mismatch.
Later Resolved - change required issue mentioning device-productidentifierinudi and THO migration; it is background only for this default Applied/Published reconciliation.
